hook_text: She raised her price... and R480 vanished from the tin. One number saw it coming.
clip_script: Monday, she lifts the maize meal price ten percent. Pap is supper and the way out does not exist: a stone. Almost nobody stops buying, and the tin fills faster. Thursday, feeling brave, she lifts the ice lollies from ten rand to twelve. Ice lollies are a treat with ways out in every direction: a feather. Sales drop from three hundred a week to two hundred and ten. It was ten rand times three hundred — three thousand rand. Now twelve rand times two hundred and ten — two thousand five hundred and twenty. She raised the price and lost four hundred and eighty rand. Stone: push price up, revenue follows. Feather: pull price down, revenue follows.
visual_style: A spaza counter with a money tin whose running total glows green on Monday and drains red on Thursday, a stone and a drifting feather hovering over the two products.
pacing: Two-beat structure — Monday win, Thursday loss — closing on the rule as a mic-drop.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to calculate elasticity and never price blind again.
